assertPublicHost resolves the hostname once (line 152) but fetch() re-resolves it independently, so a DNS-rebinding host can pass the public-address check and then be fetched at a private/loopback address.

The private-address deny list is incomplete: IPv6 NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96), 6to4 (2002::/16) and IPv4 ranges such as 192.0.0.0/24 and 198.18.0.0/15 are not blocked, so internal hosts reachable via those prefixes pass the check.

sharp() is called on untrusted input with no limitInputPixels lower than the ~268M-pixel default; a few-KB highly compressible PNG declaring e.g. 16000x16000 pixels decodes to ~1 GB per request (decompression/pixel bomb), and requests are unauthenticated and concurrent.

Every distinct upload or URL is written to the on-disk cache (original plus up to 10 thumbnails) with no eviction, quota or authentication, so any client can fill the disk by posting unique images (README admits no eviction).

Returned thumbnail URLs are built from req.protocol and the client-supplied Host header, so a request with a forged Host header gets (and may cache/propagate) URLs pointing at an attacker-controlled host.
The only URL-safety test is the private-address refusal; the 20 MB download cap, redirect refusal, fetch timeout and multipart 413 path in fetchSource/multer are never exercised.
